How to deploy Hermes Agent on a VPS with Telegram and dashboard access
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough for deploying Hermes Agent, a self-hosted personal AI assistant, on a Hostinger VPS using a one-click install. Covers initial setup, connecting to OpenRouter as the LLM provider, configuring a Telegram bot for chat, starting the persistent gateway, and accessing the Hermes dashboard via SSH port forwarding. Also demonstrates setting up cron jobs for scheduled tasks like daily tech news reports, with notes on basic security considerations.

recent_posts.title: Building a full stack AI app with Python FastAPI, Next.js and Supabase
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of a full-stack AI app architecture combining Python (FastAPI) on the backend with Next.js on the frontend and Supabase for storage and database. The app converts GitHub README files into styled landing pages using OpenAI. Key topics include why you'd use a separate Python backend alongside Next.js, handling long-running tasks with Celery background jobs, storing generated HTML artifacts in Supabase Storage vs Postgres, and polling from Next.js to surface async job results to the browser without page refresh.

recent_posts.title: Rork AI lets you build native iOS Swift apps from the browser
recent_posts.summary: Rork is an AI-powered mobile app builder with two tiers: Rork Pro (React Native/Expo for cross-platform iOS and Android) and the newer Rork Max (native iOS Swift apps built directly in the browser). Rork Max enables deep iOS integrations like widgets, Live Activities, Dynamic Island, Apple Watch, AR, and iMessage apps — features typically unavailable in cross-platform tools. A YouTube thumbnail generator app was demoed with Rork Pro, and a trip suggester app with Rork Max, both requiring only one or two prompts. Both tiers support code access, GitHub sync, environment variables, and device previews. Rork Max can simulate a full iPhone experience in the browser. Integrations include RevenueCat for payments, AI image/text generation, camera, sensors, location, haptics, and authentication.

recent_posts.title: How to run background jobs in Next.js using Trigger.dev
recent_posts.summary: Building long-running background jobs in Next.js is tricky due to serverless function timeouts. Trigger.dev solves this by letting you define tasks outside the Next.js request-response cycle, with built-in retries, queuing, observability, and real-time progress streaming to the frontend. A demo app shows a video captioning workflow: uploading to Supabase, extracting audio, transcribing with OpenAI Whisper, generating SRT files, and burning subtitles into video using FFmpeg via Trigger's built-in extensions. Tasks are split for independent retry logic, and the useRealtimeRun hook streams progress updates to the UI. The Trigger dashboard provides full observability into task runs, logs, and subtask durations.

recent_posts.title: Try Hermes Agent on VPS in 8 Minutes - Tutorial
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of setting up Hermes Agent on a VPS (Hostinger) from scratch. Covers SSH setup, user creation, installing Hermes Agent, configuring Telegram as a messaging channel, setting up web search via Firecrawl, and scheduling a daily tech news briefing using cron jobs. Also demonstrates running the gateway persistently with tmux.

recent_posts.title: How to set up OpenClaw with web search, memory, backups and email
recent_posts.summary: A practical setup guide for OpenClaw, an AI agent framework, covering four key enhancements: configuring Brave Search API for web search capabilities, setting up QMD as an improved memory backend with better retrieval and session transcript indexing, backing up the workspace folder to a private GitHub repo using Git and personal access tokens, and giving the agent its own email inbox via AgentMail for email summarization and sending. The guide also covers hosting on a Hostinger VPS and managing tool usage to avoid unnecessary API calls.

recent_posts.title: Full stack AI app architecture with Python FastAPI and Supabase
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of the tech stack for building a production-ready full-stack AI app using Python. The stack covers FastAPI for the backend, React+Vite for the frontend in a monorepo, Supabase for PostgreSQL database and file storage, Celery with Redis for background job queuing, SQLAlchemy/SQLModel as ORM, and Pydantic AI as an AI SDK abstraction. The demo app is an AI YouTube thumbnail generator that uses hybrid semantic+keyword search via pgvector embeddings. Key architectural decisions include decoupled frontend/backend, async job queuing to avoid blocking users during AI inference, and polling for job status updates.

recent_posts.title: How to build a custom mission control dashboard with OpenClaw and Supabase
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of building a custom 'mission control' dashboard using OpenClaw, an AI coding agent, to replace isolated tools like Apple Notes with an integrated personal workflow hub. The setup uses React and FastAPI on a VPS, with Supabase handling authentication, database storage (PostgreSQL), and file storage. The guide covers scaffolding the app via Telegram prompts, wiring up Supabase tables and buckets, previewing via SSH tunneling, and pushing code to GitHub. Supabase is a sponsor of the video.

recent_posts.title: Claude Code computer use lets Claude control your desktop apps on macOS
recent_posts.summary: Claude Code now supports computer use on macOS, allowing it to visually see your screen and interact with native desktop apps via mouse clicks. Implemented as an MCP server, it requires screen recording and accessibility permissions. Current limitations include browser interactions being screenshot-only (clicks require the Claude Chrome extension), and IDE support being click-only. A practical demo shows Claude Code automating an audio processing workflow in iZotope by opening files, applying a DS filter, and saving — all without any manual mouse input. The feature is in research preview and requires a Pro or Max plan.

top_posts.title: Essential SQL concepts explained
top_posts.summary: SQL is a structured query language used to manage and analyze data in databases. Understanding SQL concepts is valuable for both organizations and individual careers. Key SQL concepts include creating and managing databases, tables, and relationships, as well as performing queries to insert, update, delete, and retrieve data. Proper data structuring, using primary and foreign keys, and employing joins are essential for database efficiency. Indexing can optimize queries, and using transactions ensures data consistency. Tools and certifications like those offered by DataCamp can enhance SQL skills.

top_posts.title: Next.js 15 authentication guide best practices and common pitfalls
top_posts.summary: This post provides a comprehensive guide on implementing authentication in Next.js 15, emphasizing server-side security, proper use of cookies and tokens, and the importance of roles and permissions. It highlights best practices and pitfalls to avoid when using server components and middleware to protect routes and actions. Additionally, it underscores the benefits of using third-party services for authentication to avoid errors and save development time.

top_posts.title: AI Vibe Coding Tutorial + Workflow (Cursor, Best Practices, PRD, Rules, MCP)

It highlights the tools like Cursor, Visual Studio Code, and Windsurf, and explains the workflow for creating an app from scratch. Best practices, pitfalls to avoid, and the benefits of using AI in coding are emphasized. top_posts.title: Building Next.js apps with n8n workflow automation and VPS deployment
top_posts.summary: Demonstrates how to integrate Next.js with n8n workflow automation platform to create sophisticated applications without extensive backend coding. Shows building a CSV to JSON converter where Next.js handles the frontend while n8n processes the data transformation through visual workflows. Includes complete deployment setup using Coolify on a VPS, covering both local development and production hosting with custom domains and environment configuration.

top_posts.title: AI-based scraping made simple with Scraperless
top_posts.summary: Traditional web scraping required manually pinpointing data within HTML structures and managing infrastructure for requests. AI-based solutions like Scraperless simplify this process by allowing users to describe the desired data without specifying HTML details. Scraperless utilizes free-form prompts to determine scraping targets and offers integration via API keys, allowing developers to incorporate it into their applications seamlessly. Results are available in formats like CSV, making data handling straightforward with minimal user effort.
